Name: The Longest Year
Author: sonofskywalker3
Description:
[size=6][b]The Longest Year[/b][/size]
[size=4][i]Restore the Community Center within a single year — or the Junimos rewind the seasons and you begin again, a little stronger.[/i][/size]

[color=yellow][b]BETA (0.16.167).[/b] Feature-complete and stable in testing. What it needs now is your feedback on difficulty, pricing, and pacing — see the bottom of this page.[/color]

[color=yellow][b]This is the last big engine update.[/b] From here the plan is bug fixes and balance passes driven by your feedback, and then work begins on the story. So this is the version to tell me what is wrong with.[/color]

[line]

[size=5][b]What's New in 0.16.167[/b][/size]

[b]Spend JP mid-loop, keep the Junimos' own gifts, and a board that counts every slot.[/b]
[list]
[*][b]JP Boosts.[/b] The Junimo statue on your farm now has three tabs. Boosts sells eighteen this-loop buys for JP: tomorrow's rain or storm, a guaranteed lucky day, a free late night, a week of extra forage, fish, crop, mine, monster, machine, animal or all-round rolls that stack with the weekly theme, a faster walk, a season of cheaper shops, faster friendships, extra energy, a skill level on the spot (temporary, price climbs with each one), or an elevator stop you have not earned yet. Active shows what is running and when it ends; Plan shows every keep's price and what the locked ones still need.[/*]
[*][b]Gifts of the Junimos.[/b] A new shrine category: Keep Greenhouse (put back where you left it), Keep Quarry Bridge, Keep Boulder Cleared, Keep Minecarts and Keep Bus Unlocked. Each is offered once you have earned that room's reward this loop; the first costs 1,000 JP and every Gift you own raises the price of the rest by 1,000, up to 5,000. The room's bundles stay on the board and still pay.[/*]
[*][b]Three new weekly themes: Spelunking, Artisan and Kitchen.[/b] Their goals match by item kind anywhere on the board. Spelunking doubles monster drops one time in ten but slows machines; Artisan speeds machines but weakens cooked food; Kitchen gives animals a chance at a second product but monsters hit harder. Eight themes, still two cards a week, and the weekly JP bonus is now paid goal by goal.[/*]
[*][b]Keep your wallet items and Stardrops.[/b] Eighteen new keeps, one per wallet item, one each for Bear's Knowledge and Spring Onion Mastery, and one per Stardrop source. Plus a Garden Pot recipe keep.[/*]
[*][b]The board counts every slot.[/b] A donation credits one bundle, a bundle with a repeated item needs every slot, and a Winter win needs a truly finished Center. Bundles roll from the full pool of their kind with no item asked twice, seasonal forage bundles ask only for their season, Night Fishing asks only for night fish, and legendary fish and year-two crops can appear at low odds. Every item has a first week it can exist, so no gate asks for what you cannot reach.[/*]
[*][b]Fixes.[/b] Keep Bus Unlocked now actually runs the bus from day 1 (the Vault bundles stay on the board and still pay). Heart-event invitations send again every loop, so 8 and 10 heart events are reachable after a rewind. Keep Horse waits for a stable. Stardew Valley Expanded saves keep season pity. A toggle to re-send the Better Start gift each loop (on by default).[/*]
[*]0.16.18 to 0.16.166 were internal builds; this is the first release since 0.16.17.[/*]
[/list]
Coming from 0.15.0 or earlier? 0.16.0 added ten independent [b]Difficulty[/b] dials in the settings menu and made every bundle apply pressure at the season checkpoints, which makes the year harder at every difficulty. Details in the changelog on GitHub.

[line]

[size=5][b]What it is[/b][/size]
The Longest Year turns Stardew's first year into a roguelite loop. Each season, you must give back enough of the land's bounty to the old Community Center hall. Fall short by a season's end and the Junimos turn time back to Spring 1 — the world resets, but the strength you've earned, and the power your offerings have banked, can carry forward. Restore the whole Center inside one year to break the loop for good.

[size=5][b]Features[/b][/size]
[list]
[*][b]Seasonal time-loop.[/b] Each season has a donation minimum. Miss it and the year unwinds to Spring 1.[/*]
[*][b]Junimo Points.[/b] Donations earn JP — scaled by rarity and by how late in the year you give. JP banks across loops.[/*]
[*][b]The Junimo Shrine.[/b] Spend JP on upgrades that let you hold on to some of what you gained: skill levels, tool tiers, recipes, buildings, a kept pet, the power books you have read, your wallet items and Stardrops, the Junimos' own gifts (greenhouse, quarry bridge, boulder, minecarts, bus), and more.[/*]
[*][b]JP Boosts.[/b] The Junimo statue on your farm sells this-loop edges for JP: tomorrow's rain or a lucky day, a free late night, stacking forage/fish/crop/mine/drop chances, a faster walk, a season of cheaper shops, faster friendships, extra energy, a skill level on the spot, or an elevator stop you have not earned yet. An Active tab shows what is running and a Plan tab shows what each keep still needs.[/*]
[*][b]Weekly themes.[/b] Each week, pick one of two themes (Foraging, Farming, Fishing, Mining, Mixed, Spelunking, Artisan, Kitchen) for a bonus and a paired liability. Goals follow the season gate and the weekly bonus is paid per goal.[/*]
[*][b]Carryover surfaces.[/b] A Bundle Log book that tracks each season's goals, a Cookbook and Craftbook to bank recipes, and a Junimo Stash chest that survives resets.[/*]
[*][b]A real intro.[/b] Lewis greets you on the porch; a Junimo explains the loop. Then the run begins.[/*]
[*][b]A starved Traveling Cart.[/b] Joja has squeezed the merchant's suppliers — the cart carries [b]one item[/b] per visit until you unlock more stalls with the [b]Cart Stall[/b] upgrades (and Cart Whisperer previews what's coming). Prefer the full vanilla cart? Turn off [font=Courier New]LimitTravelingCartStock[/font].[/*]
[*][b]The town half-remembers.[/b] Villagers you have spent a lot of time with across loops occasionally say something uncanny. Rare, no gameplay effect, and it never explains itself. Toggle in Features.[/*]
[*][b]Break the loop.[/b] Finish the Center in a year to win — then keep playing or start fresh.[/*]
[/list]
[size=5][b]Requirements[/b][/size]
[list]
[*]Stardew Valley 1.6+ (PC)[/*]
[*]SMAPI 4.0.0+[/*]
[*]A [b]new save[/b] on the [b]Standard farm[/b][/*]
[/list]
[size=5][b]Install[/b][/size]
[list=1]
[*]Install SMAPI 4.0.0 or newer.[/*]
[*]Unzip into your [font=Courier New]Stardew Valley/Mods[/font] folder.[/*]
[*]Launch through SMAPI and [b]start a new game on the Standard farm[/b]. Farm-type and intro options are handled for you.[/*]
[*][b]Community Center Bundles[/b] under [b]New → Advanced Options[/b] defaults to [b]TLY Custom[/b]: every loop rolls a fresh board from the vanilla + remix pools plus the mod's own authored bundles. Prefer the game's own board (or another bundle mod's)? Pick [b]Normal[/b] or [b]Remixed[/b] there instead — the mod keeps that board and re-rolls it the same way on every reset. ([font=Courier New]BundleSource[/font] in the config/GMCM is the default for new games and switches an existing save at its next reset.)
[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/47192/47192-1787355673-935410882.png[/img][/*]
[/list]
[size=5][b]Limitations (beta)[/b][/size]
[list]
[*]PC only — no Android port yet.[/*]
[*]Standard farm only.[/*]
[*]A run can only be started from a new game (other saves load normally and are left untouched).[/*]
[*]Intro cutscene and dialogue are a first pass.[/*]
[*]Multiplayer untested.[/*]
[/list]
[size=5][b]Is this a bug?[/b][/size]

A few things get reported often enough to be worth answering up front.

[b]Demetrius never shows up about the cave, I just get a popup asking mushrooms or bats.[/b]
That is the mod, working as intended. His scene plays once per playthrough; from the second loop on, walking into the farm cave gives you the choice directly instead of replaying a cutscene you have already watched. The mushrooms-or-bats decision is re-offered every loop because the rewind clears it.

[b]The Traveling Cart only has one item.[/b]
Also intended. Joja is squeezing the merchant's suppliers, and the Cart Stall upgrades at the Junimo Shrine add slots back. If you would rather have the full cart, turn off LimitTravelingCartStock in the config.

[b]I did the Egg Hunt and now Lewis will not let me do it again today.[/b]
Since 0.14.1, a festival's main event runs once per day. Festivals in this mod do not end your day, so you can walk out and back in - which used to restart the whole festival and let the hunt be repeated for the prize. The stalls, the shop and everyone at the festival still work on a repeat visit. A new loop is a clean slate: as far as the valley is concerned the festival has not happened yet, so you get to do it again.

[b]A bundle is asking for silver or gold on something that cannot have a quality.[/b]
That was a bug and it is fixed. Quality is only ever asked for on things the game itself gives quality to (crop harvests, rod-caught fish, spawned forage). Existing boards pick the change up at the next reset.

[b]A weekly goal ticked off without me donating anything.[/b]
Fixed in 0.14.0. Finishing a bundle that only needs some of its listed items used to mark the rest as filled, which credited goals you never handed in. A goal now waits for the real donation.

[b]I bought Keep Bus Unlocked and the Vault bundles are still on the board.[/b]
Intended. The gift keeps the bus and the desert open from day 1; the Vault bundles are still part of restoring the Center, still have to be paid, and still earn JP. Completing them again does not replay the repair scene. Every Gift of the Junimos works this way.

[b]The skill level I bought at the statue was gone after the rewind.[/b]
Intended. Crash Course levels are temporary: they last the loop, never reach level 10, and cannot be kept. Only levels you earn open the Keep Level rows on a Fail night.

[b]Elevator Pass says "Enter the mine first", or a weather boost says "Not now".[/b]
Both intended. The pass extends the elevator from wherever it already reaches, so it needs one trip into the mine first. Rain Dance and Storm Call are refused on day 28 and the day before a festival, because the game forces sunshine on those mornings and the JP would be wasted.

[b]My enchanted sword lost its enchantments in the Junimo Stash.[/b]
Fixed since 0.16.7. Tools and weapons in the stash keep their enchantments, forged gems, bait and tackle across the rewind.

Anything not on this list, please do report - the bugs tab is read.

[line]

[size=5][b]Difficulty[/b][/size]
Ten independent difficulty dials live in the mod's settings menu (GMCM) under [b]Difficulty[/b]. There is no overall difficulty setting: turn up only what you want turned up. Every dial has four steps, [b]Easy / Normal / Hard / Extreme[/b], and every one starts on [b]Normal[/b], which is the balance the mod ships with. Changing nothing changes nothing.

[b]Changes take effect on your next loop, not straight away.[/b] The dials are stamped onto your save when a loop begins, so the year you are already playing keeps the rules it started under.
[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/47192/47192-1787870999-2094236733.png[/img]

[b]What the bundles ask for[/b]
[list]
[*][b]Stack size.[/b] How many of an item a slot asks for, up to 99. Money bundles are never affected.[/*]
[*][b]Quality asks.[/b] How often a slot wants a silver or gold star. Items the game never gives a star to are still never asked for at quality, at any step.[/*]
[*][b]Required slots.[/b] How many of a bundle's shown items you must actually donate. Hard asks for one more, Easy one fewer, Extreme asks for all of them.[/*]
[*][b]Item rarity.[/b] Weights bundles toward harder items: rarer, later in the year, or needing a keg or a press. [b]TLY Custom bundles only[/b] (see below).[/*]
[/list]
[b]What you carry between loops[/b]
[list]
[*][b]Junimo Points earned.[/b] Scales every JP award, so progress across loops is faster or slower. The season ramp keeps its shape, so late-season donating is still worth the most.[/*]
[*][b]Shrine prices.[/b] Scales what upgrades cost at the Junimo Shrine.[/*]
[*][b]Starting gold.[/b] Scales the [font=Courier New]StartingMoney[/font] value rather than replacing it. Extreme starts you with nothing.[/*]
[*][b]Starting cart slots.[/b] How many items the Traveling Cart offers before you buy any Cart Stall upgrade. On Hard and Extreme the cart is empty until you buy Cart Stall I.[/*]
[*][b]Hold and pity prices.[/b] Scales the JP price of keeping your board on a Fail night, and of accepting the Junimos' offer to ease a season. The first of each stays free at every step.[/*]
[*][b]Season pity.[/b] How readily the Junimos ease a season you keep failing. Easy helps sooner and more, Hard waits longer and helps less, Extreme never helps. Your failed-season counting keeps running either way, so turning it back up picks up where it left off.[/*]
[/list]
[b]One dial does not work on vanilla boards.[/b] Item rarity applies to [b]TLY Custom[/b] bundles only, because changing which item a vanilla bundle asks for would be changing the bundle. Stack size, quality asks and required slots all work on vanilla Standard and Remixed boards too.

[font=Courier New]tly_difficulty[/font] in the SMAPI console prints what your save is actually running under, including anything you have changed since your last loop. Please attach it to any balance report.

[line]

[size=5][b]Switching bundle source later[/b][/size]
You are not locked into the board you picked when you started. [b]Bundle source[/b] in the mod's settings menu (GMCM) is one setting with three choices, and you can move an existing save between any of them:
[list]
[*][b]TLY Custom[/b] - the mod composes a fresh board every loop from the vanilla and remix pools plus its own authored bundles.[/*]
[*][b]Normal[/b] - the game's own standard bundle layout, re-rolled the same way each loop.[/*]
[*][b]Remixed[/b] - the game's own remixed layout, likewise.[/*]
[/list]
Another bundle mod's board is covered by Normal or Remixed: whatever the game generates is what the mod keeps.

Like the difficulty dials, a switch applies at your [b]next loop[/b], not straight away. The year you are already playing keeps the board it started with.

[b]Keeping your board on a Fail night works on all three.[/b] If you hold, you get the same board back next loop whichever source it came from.

[line]

[size=5][b]Tuning[/b][/size]
The [b]Features[/b] section of the settings menu turns individual parts of the mod off or tunes them, and changes there apply straight away:
[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/47192/47192-1787870999-1916723524.png[/img]
Everything difficulty-related lives in [font=Courier New]config.json[/font] — JP values, per-season multipliers, completion bonuses, starting gold, and per-bundle quotas. Tweak freely and tell me what felt right. [font=Courier New]LimitTravelingCartStock[/font] (also in GMCM) turns the one-item Traveling Cart cap off if you'd rather have the full vanilla cart. [font=Courier New]BundleSource[/font] (also in GMCM): [font=Courier New]Engine[/font] = the mod's own board every loop (the new-game [b]TLY Custom[/b] choice); [font=Courier New]Vanilla[/font] = keep the game's Standard/Remixed board (or another bundle mod's, e.g. Challenging Community Center Bundles) and re-roll it the same way on each reset. Takes effect at the next reset; the new-game dropdown sets it per save. [font=Courier New]BundleHoldCosts[/font] sets the JP price of keeping the same bundle board on a Fail night by consecutive holds (default 0, 50, 100, 200, 300; reshuffling resets the count). Season pity ([font=Courier New]PityThreshold[/font] 5, [font=Courier New]PityQuotaStep[/font] 0.10, [font=Courier New]PityQuotaFloor[/font] 0.50, [font=Courier New]PityTrimPerStep[/font] 2, [font=Courier New]PityCosts[/font] 0/50/100/200/300, [font=Courier New]PityEnabled[/font]) tunes when and how much the Junimos offer to ease a season you keep failing.

[line]

[size=5][b]Feedback wanted[/b][/size]
[list]
[*][b]Difficulty[/b] — are the seasonal minimums fair? Which wall hit hardest?[/*]
[*][b]Pricing[/b] — do JP earnings and shrine costs feel balanced? What did you save for first?[/*]
[*][b]Pacing[/b] — how many loops before it "clicked"? Did carryover make later loops feel stronger?[/*]
[*][b]Bugs[/b] — please attach your [font=Courier New]SMAPI-latest.txt[/font] (from [font=Courier New]Stardew Valley/ErrorLogs/[/font]).[/*]
[/list]
[line]

[size=5][b]Art wanted[/b][/size]
The mod leans on vanilla sprites throughout. If anyone would enjoy making some custom book/sprite artwork (the Cookbook and Craftbook especially), I'd genuinely love to accept it and credit you. Drop a note in the comments.

[i]Banner art by [b]cwybabiesucks[/b] — thank you![/i]

[line]

[size=5][b]Translations[/b][/size]
As of 0.11.60, every player-visible string in the mod lives in a JSON file ([font=Courier New]i18n/default.json[/font]) — the mod is fully translatable with no DLL edits or rebuilds. See [url=https://github.com/sonofskywalker3/TheLongestYear/blob/master/docs/TRANSLATING.md]TRANSLATING.md[/url] for how to add a language. If you translate it, let us know (Nexus DM or GitHub issue) and we'll link your work from the mod page.
